title: CANcestry T2 Virtual Bench CAN Fault Evidence (v0.1.0)
description: Schema for the H-10 (issue #62) T2 CAN fault-scenario evidence artifacts t2_busoff_001.json and t2_crc_001.json, produced by hw/virtual-bench/t2_fault_common.py and its scenario clients. Sibling of hw-t2-evidence-0.1.0 (retention) with the DELIBERATE differences recorded here: (1) oracle_id is the literal 'none' - issue #62 assigns no OR-XXX to Bus-Off recovery timing or CRC error handling, and HwAGENTS.md rule 3's oracle rule is satisfied by the honest disposition: the traceability ledger rows stay sim-pending / CL0 and the artifact alone cannot promote them (the ledger checker alone permits passing rows, and only with a registered oracle); (2) the evidence hash chain is ELF + bridge (monitor client) + injector + trace - these scenarios use no FMU: the CAN bus medium is the fault injector, so OpenModelica/FMPy are not producers, are not pinned and contribute no inherited gap (renode stays TCL2 and its gap is inherited verbatim); (3) the pending disposition fixes a fixed injection boundary (t = 10 ms) and a fixed 50 ms window with a 100 us master step. Kept in lockstep with the retention schema's pending/pairing discipline.

case_id.description: The two H-10 CAN fault scenarios (issue #62): Bus-Off recovery (t2_busoff_001) and CRC error handling (t2_crc_001).

requirement_id.description: ISO 11898-2 CAN interface conformance; the Bus-Off and CRC handling of the gateway node is exercised on the virtual bench.

oracle_id.description: Documented H-10 deviation: no registered oracle covers Bus-Off timing or CRC handling (issue #62: 'Oracle: none'). The ledger rows stay sim-pending / CL0 regardless of an executed run; this artifact never promotes a requirement.

status.description: pending: no executed T2 run for this scenario (foundation). passing: a deterministic executed run backs every claim. 'failing' does not exist: a failed run aborts before evidence is written (fail-closed, t2_fault_common.py).

provisional.description: True: the claim is never final without T4 bench correlation and, per issue #62, the rows stay sim-pending / CL0 for H-Phase 2 regardless.

credibility_level.description: Pending artifacts are CL0. An executed run may record its achieved credibility but cannot exceed CL1 in H-10 (no independent oracle; CL2 requires one and CL3 is bench-only per HwAGENTS.md rule 4).

pending_reason.description: Mandatory while pending and forbidden when passing; must name the exact deferral (the first executing run of this very scenario, issue #62).

duration_us.description: 50 ms scenario window (issue #62: the T2 timeline visualizes 0..50 ms; 704 us of Bus-Off recovery from a 10 ms injection fits with wide margin).

fault.description: Which fault the injector applies at inject_at_us. Brownout is OUT of H-10 scope by constraint (H-11, HS-01/HS-02).

inject_at_us.description: Issue #62: the fault is injected at t = 10 ms.

master_step_us.description: The H-07 bridge contract master step; the injection lands exactly on a master-step boundary (10 ms).

seed.description: Fixed Renode seed (HwAGENTS.md rule 5), equal to fmi_bridge.FIXED_SEED.

modification.description: T2 executes the v1.0.0 ELF as-is (issue #62 constraint 1).

inherited_validation_gap.description: The renode TCL2 gap is ALWAYS inherited (renode is a producer of every form of this artifact); can_fault_injector is TCL1 and carries no gap; OpenModelica/FMPy are not producers of these scenarios and contribute nothing.

columns.description: Bus-Off scenario traces the alive counter; the CRC scenario traces the firmware CRC error counter.

injection_us.description: Injector-stamped acceptance time of the fault command (exact emulation time; the injection boundary is a master-step multiple).

detection_us.description: Symbol-hook stamp of the firmware's fault-detection function entry (t2_can_busoff_detect / t2_can_crc_detect).

recovery_request_us.description: Bus-Off only: .resc CCCR write hook stamp of the firmware clearing CCCR.INIT (the ISO 11898-1 recovery request).

recovery_us.description: Bus-Off only: symbol-hook stamp of t2_can_busoff_recover (the firmware recovery action).

bus_active_us.description: Bus-Off only: injector stamp of the medium release, exactly 128 * 11 recessive bits (704 us at 2 Mbit/s) after the recovery request.

crc_ack_us.description: CRC only: .resc IR write hook stamp of the firmware acknowledging the error-logging interrupt (IR.ELO W1C).

crc_cleared_us.description: CRC only: injector stamp of the CRC condition leaving the medium (equals the acknowledge time by the injector's single-writer semantics).

hashes.description: Evidence hash chain (issue #62 deliverable 10, adapted): ELF hash + bridge hash + injector hash + trace hash. No FMU: the CAN bus medium is the injector.

invariants.description: The scenario's asserted invariants, checked in-run by t2_fault_common.py; the schema enforces the structural contract only.

credibility_level.description: An executed run without a registered oracle cannot record more than CL1 in H-10; the traceability row stays sim-pending / CL0 regardless (issue #62: no ledger promotion).

pending_reason.description: The deferral must name the H-10 issue (first executing run of this scenario).

bus_recovery_sequence_us.description: 128 * 11 recessive bits at the HW-FR-003 nominal 2 Mbit/s.

recovery_action_delta_us.description: recovery_us - detection_us of THIS executed run.

recovery_action_limit_us.description: Issue #62 timing limit: 128 * 11 bit times (704 us at 2 Mbit/s).

recovery_action_within_limit.description: The issue invariant: recovery action strictly inside the 128 * 11 bit-times bound; a violated bound aborts the run before evidence is written, so a committed artifact can only record true.

crc_error_counter_at_end.description: Issue #62: the firmware's CRC error counter incremented at least once; zero would be a firmware defect and the run fails closed instead of writing evidence.

firmware_crashed.description: Issue #62: the firmware handled the CRC error without crashing (run_complete = 1 and the alive counter advanced); a crash fails the run before any artifact is written.
